qualitative_or_quantitative_description.value: The deformation mode of M1 is planar slip of dislocations; the highly coherent κ-carbides are cut (sheared) by dislocations, destroying the coherency relationship and softening the glide plane, which reduces the work-hardening rate of M1-30. The homogeneous precipitation of κ-carbides prevents refinement of the slip band and reduces the work-hardening index of M1 after aging.

slip_behavior.value: Planar dislocation slip (SFE ~70 mJ/m^2); the slip-band spacing of M2 is significantly smaller than that of M1, but both steels deform by planar slip.

phase_evolution.value: Supersaturated austenite matrix decomposes into solute-depleted and solute-enriched regions; when sufficient driving force is attained the solute-enriched regions transform into L-ordered domains and carbon ordering forms κ-carbides (generally attributed to spinodal decomposition). In the Ti/V-free M1 matrix with homogeneous chemical composition, κ-carbides exhibit a uniform distribution.

interface_notes.value: In M1-30 no (Ti, V)C carbides are present (the table shows '-' for M1-30); κ-carbides are the only intragranular precipitate and are highly coherent with the matrix.

unmapped_findings: The stacking fault energy (SFE) of M1 was calculated as approximately 70 mJ/m^2 (M2 ~78 mJ/m^2), indicating that the deformation mode of the material is dislocation slip; Ti and V have little influence on the SFE.
The number density of κ-carbides in M1-30 is around 7 × 10^22 m^-3.

The κ-carbide shearing strengthening in M1-30 is unchanged in nature from that of κ-carbides that precipitate uniformly; the yield strength increase of M1 after aging is mainly due to shear strengthening of the κ-carbides.

In M1-30 there are no (Ti, V)C carbides (Table 3 reports '-' for M1 for both solution-treated and 30 h aged conditions); only κ-carbides are present with volume fraction 7.4 ± 3.4 % and mean radius 10.8 ± 6.2 nm.
Adding Ti and V does not alter the austenitic phase composition of the low-density steel but refines the grain size (M1 42.4 ± 7.8 μm → M2 32.3 ± 10.4 μm in the solution-treated state).
